tagline: Find the roles worth your time—and see exactly why before you apply.
shortDescription: JobPilot turns application fatigue into a transparent decision loop: discover nearby and Remote roles, prioritize three next decisions, understand the evidence, open the original employer destination, and track progress locally—without auto-apply or hidden score adjustments.
inspiration: Application fatigue is decision fatigue: repeated searches, manual comparison, employer-link hunting, and disconnected tracking still leave a job seeker unsure which application deserves the next hour.
problem: Discovery, prioritization, explanation, employer handoff, and tracking are fragmented across separate surfaces.
whatItDoes: Connects DISCOVER → PRIORITIZE → UNDERSTAND → APPLY → TRACK around a transparent three-role shortlist.
howItWorks: Gemma 4 12B owns bounded semantic interpretation, deterministic AI Fit V2.2 owns all numeric scoring and receipts, and four provenance-bound gpt-5.6-sol reviews were prepared through Codex from frozen synthetic evidence.
nearbyDiscovery: Profile-configured city, distance, and work-mode preferences drive deterministic nearby and Remote labels without changing technical Fit Score.
resumeAwarePrioritization: The local edition parses a resume in memory, asks the user to confirm structured evidence, stores it browser-locally, and uses loopback gemma4:12b; the public deployment accepts no resume.
directEmployerDestination: Only an explicit verified trust state uses Apply on Employer Site; the synthetic public destination disables submission and never auto-marks Applied.
scoreReceiptVerifier: Web, API, and CLI surfaces independently reproduce canonicalization, exact micro-point arithmetic, evidence/source hashes, and tamper failure.
gemmaUse: Primary semantic model for extraction, grouping, evidence matching, equivalence, summaries, and uncertainty; cached prepared analyses in public review and live loopback only in the local edition.
gpt56Use: Four gpt-5.6-sol outputs prepared through Codex: strategy, challenge, ambiguity review, and comparison. They are not live runtime calls and cannot change a score.
zeroApiRuntime: 0 OpenAI API requests and $0 OpenAI API cost.
codexUse: Golden Path, scorer, UX, privacy boundary, receipt verifier, prepared review integration, QA, coverage freeze, defect timeline, and release evidence.
lessons: Trust comes from progressive proof, explicit model boundaries, reproducible arithmetic, and disciplined claim limits.
privacy: Synthetic public data, no account, no production database, no OpenAI key, no public resume upload, no application submission.
limitations: Processed-portfolio coverage only; Fit Score is not a hiring probability; public product data is synthetic. The n=5 usability result is directional: all participants completed the traditional condition first, so practice or order effects may contribute.
buildWeekExtension: Added the no-login Golden Path, application-fatigue story, nearby discovery, transparent shortlist, private resume isolation, concise detail, comparison, safe handoff, tracker, verifier, GPT review surfaces, tour, Trust Lab, defect timeline, coverage proof, and study workflow.
testingInstructions: Landing → Today’s Shortlist → Northstar detail → receipt FULLY_REPRODUCED → tamper INVALID → synthetic employer destination → return and explicitly mark Preparing → Trust Lab → Coverage Proof.
teamInformation: Single entrant; confirm the authenticated Devpost profile and owner-visible team label before submission.
finalProductRc: Distinct public landing and For You app home; visible Why these three rationale; visual decision, dimension, experience, practical-fit, Evidence, Score Proof, and collapsed exact Technical Ledger; restrained motion and complete states.
studyV2: jobpilot-decision-utility.v2 uses Analytics Operations Engineer and Data Enablement Engineer, counterbalances role assignment, requires primer comprehension, and excludes PREVIEW and PILOT from final evidence. Five authentic Final sessions achieved the minimum sample; condition order was fixed traditional-first.
potentialImpact: In a moderated directional usability study with five participants, median task time was 18 seconds with JobPilot versus 39 seconds with a traditional posting. Factual accuracy was 100% versus 75%; confidence was 6.0 versus 3.8 and clarity was 6.2 versus 3.6 out of 7. Everyone completed the traditional condition first, so results may include an order effect.
